result.title: Production Kill Switch Goal

facts.text: This setup goal produces research, an approved design, an execution plan, and one GitHub issue; it does not implement production kill-switch code.
The design targets a global bolt-v3 LiveNode/runtime kill switch for configured accounts, instruments, and strategies, not a strategy-local kill path.
The kill switch workflow is detect, latch, stop new risk, cancel outstanding order risk, flatten open positions, verify flat/no-open-risk state, then require authorized manual reset.
The halt state is durable and includes at least armed, halting, cancelling, halted, flattening, flat, and failed_manual_intervention states.
Durable halt evidence records the trigger, reason set, NT source timestamps, operator/manual trigger identity where applicable, action attempts, reconciliation proof, and manual reset evidence.
After restart, missing, stale, corrupt, or unresolved halt evidence causes the runtime to fail closed instead of resuming risk admission.
The first design includes loss-governor breach, manual operator kill, stale or missing NT proof, reconciliation mismatch, cancel/flatten failure, and future extension triggers.

Once the halt latch is active, all new entry and replace risk is blocked globally; ordinary risk-reducing exits remain under ordinary caps, and verified kill-switch forced reductions use a separate proof-bound admission/action class.

Cancel routing enumerates outstanding order risk from NT-owned state, including open, inflight, pending-cancel, emulated, algorithm-managed, contingent, and accepted-but-not-terminal orders, and routes cancellation through NT APIs only while tracking accepted, rejected, expired, filled-race, and retry outcomes.

Flatten routing enumerates open positions from NT-owned state and submits configured reduce-only or forced-exit orders through NT order construction and submit paths only; forced reductions must be bound to halt/position proof and cannot rely on ordinary submit caps.
Flatten handling covers partial fills, stale position state, unknown side, unsupported instrument, thin book, rejected order, and timeout cases without claiming flat unless NT state proves it.

The design researches pinned NautilusTrader RiskEngine trading-state support and uses the safe NT trading-state path if accessible; otherwise it documents the gap and relies on local fail-closed admission blocking.
Reconciliation proof requires NT state to show no outstanding order risk, no non-flat positions, and no pending entry risk before the halt may reach flat.
If mandatory reconciliation proof is unavailable, stale, or contradictory, the system stays halted or moves to failed_manual_intervention and requires operator action.
Operator controls include manual kill, authorized manual reset with tamper-evident evidence, redacted event logs, a runbook, and a no-submit or dry-run kill drill path.
All runtime values for retries, timeouts, flatten templates, allowed accounts, allowed instruments, and reset requirements are owned by TOML config with no runtime hardcodes.
Source fences prevent strategy-local kill-switch logic, direct venue kill calls, and submit/cancel/flatten paths that bypass the global kill-switch boundary.

The verification plan covers unit state-machine tests, durable-store failure tests, cancel/fill race integration tests across all outstanding-order surfaces, forced-reduction flatten/reconciliation tests, restart/recovery tests, reset-authorization tests, source-fence checks, and a no-submit end-to-end kill drill.
Any tiny-capital live drill is explicitly out of scope for this setup goal and requires separate approval after no-submit proof exists.
The design approval quorum is at least four of six external reviewers, with Claude and Gemini mandatory; blocking findings must be resolved before issue creation.
The GitHub issue is a single phased issue containing the approved design, production invariants, implementation phases, verification matrix, model-review evidence, and explicit dependencies.
The design identifies which implementation steps depend on PR #480 landing and avoids presenting PR #480-dependent live wiring as ready before main contains the required boundary.
